newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia awaits word on Busang negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia awaits word on Busang negotiations.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Thursday he was still awaiting word from Canadian companies Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp before the February 17 deadline for reporting on their Busang gold find negotiations.
"They are still negotiating on Busang. I have not met with them yet. I will wait until the deadline on February 17," Sudjana told reporters.
The government told both companies last month to settle with their Indonesian partners before getting the go-ahead to further explore and develop the huge Busang find in West Kalimantan province.
Bre-X, which estimates Busang holds at least 57 million ounces of gold, has said it is confident it will meet the deadline.
Sudjana also said he supported efforts by two state-owned companies to get involved in the Busang development on Borneo island. But he said they would have to get Finance Ministry permission.
Gold and nickel mining company PT Aneka Tambang and major tin producer PT Tambang Timah have both said they wished to be involved.

Erry Riana, president director of Tambang Timah, told Reuters on Thursday his company wanted a significant stake based on a legal framework. But he said further developments would have to await next Monday's deadline.
Aneka Tambang said on Thursday it had also told the government it was interested in participating in Busang.

"We have sent a letter to the Mines and Energy Minister. We have also talked with Finance Ministry officials over our intention to be involved in Busang," Aneka Tambang president director Darmoko Slamet told reporters.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to partner Barrick, and the Mines and Energy Ministry said in December they had agreed to split Busang, with 22.5 percent going to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick and the rest to the government.

Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought a 50-percent stake in two companies with minority interests in two of the Busang areas.
Barrick has an alliance with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardijanti Rukmana.
Tambang Timah has said it was holding talks with Hasan over an equity participation in Busang.
